parsed.hypothesis_statement: For a synthetic parametric strategy with all non-threshold parameters held fixed, increasing the signal-entry threshold monotonically decreases the number of executed trades because threshold gating admits a nested subset of signal observations.
parsed.hypothesis_rationale: If the entry rule executes only when a scalar signal exceeds its threshold, any observation admitted at a higher threshold must also be admitted at a lower threshold, absent changes to other parameters. Testing the monotonic relation across a prespecified threshold grid isolates the threshold gate from other strategy settings; violations would indicate interactions such as stateful position constraints, execution logic, or non-nested signal definitions.

requirements.label: Generate identical synthetic signal paths across a prespecified grid of signal thresholds while holding non-threshold parameters and random seed fixed.
Measure trade counts by threshold and test the prespecified monotonic nested-admission relationship.
Execute the fixed synthetic strategy specification for each threshold using the same simulated paths and execution assumptions.
